description: Language-neutral wire conformance fixtures for the heddle v1 wire contract. See README.md.

fixtures.description: TaskMessage with every default written out explicitly.
Every TaskMessage field set; non-ASCII text and mixed JSON value types in input.
Underscore-prefixed frame keys (_trace_context and an arbitrary _x_custom) must survive round-trip unchanged (DESIGN_INVARIANTS #22).
A body key unknown to this receiver (e.g. added by a newer sender) is accepted. A receiver may drop it on re-serialization; it must not reject the message.
Successful TaskResult; occurred_at and recorded_at differ.
Failed TaskResult: output null, error set, degraded_modes in metadata.
Timestamps with microsecond precision, which is what the Python runtime emits for generated times. Parsers must accept fractional seconds.
Integer fields written as integral floats (420.0, 12.0) are accepted, as JSON Schema's integer allows; they compare equal to the integers. Emit plain integers.
OrchestratorGoal with context and request_id.
occurred_at carries a non-UTC offset (+02:00); it is the same instant as recorded_at. Compare as instants; the Python runtime re-emits the offset as given.
payload_type is required.
payload must be a JSON object.
A top-level key that is neither declared nor _-prefixed is rejected (catches misspelled fields).
occurred_at must be an RFC 3339 date-time.
occurred_at/recorded_at must carry a UTC offset; a local time without one is ambiguous.
An explicit null timestamp is invalid. Omit the field instead; a receiver then fills it (see README, Comparison rules).
Timestamps are RFC 3339 strings, not epoch numbers.

A member name repeated in one object (here payload_type, once core.TaskMessage and once events.Event) makes the text not I-JSON. Parsers disagree on which value wins, so the message is rejected before any schema runs.
The I-JSON rule applies at every depth: a repeated name inside payload.input rejects the whole message at the frame layer.
NaN (or Infinity) is not JSON and not I-JSON; some parsers accept it anyway. The message is rejected at the frame layer.
TaskMessage.worker_type is required.
TaskMessage.input must be a JSON object.
model_tier must be one of local, standard, frontier.
status must be one of pending, processing, completed, failed.
Integer fields (processing_time_ms, token_usage values) must be JSON integers, not numeric strings.
OrchestratorGoal.instruction is required.
A frame-valid message whose payload_type has no registered body is rejected at dispatch (Python: KeyError from get_payload_model).
